code: # \donttest{ ## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed ## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error th <- datasets::Theoph th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject) subjects <- unique(th$Subject) data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,                                condition = th$Subject)) ## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) init <- c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5))  ## four starts: the first at init, the others perturbed best <- msem(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, fits = 4) best$multistart #>   start    value converged iterations    gradient tries stop failures error #> 1     1 359.4032      TRUE         10 0.002975526     1 <NA>           <NA> #> 2     2 359.4032      TRUE         11 0.002859698     1 <NA>           <NA> #> 3     3 359.4032      TRUE         14 0.000496391     1 <NA>           <NA> #> 4     4 359.4032      TRUE         11 0.001513915     1 <NA>           <NA> #>   boundary #> 1          #> 2          #> 3          #> 4          plotValues(best)  # } if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## 20 starts, four fits at a time best <- msem(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, fits = 20, cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 1)) plotValues(best) } # }

code: # \donttest{   ## Generate a prediction function      times <- 0:5   grid <- data.frame(name = "A", time = times, row.names = paste0("p", times))   x <- Xd(grid, condition = "C1")      pars <- structure(rep(0, nrow(grid)), names = row.names(grid))      ## Simulate data   data.list <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {     prediction <- x(times, pars + rnorm(length(pars), 0, 1))     transform(as.data.frame(prediction), sigma = 1)   })      data <- as.datalist(do.call(rbind, data.list))      ## Generate objective function based on data and model   ## Then fit the data and plot the result   obj <- normL2(data, x)   myfit <- trust(obj, pars, rinit = 1, rmax = 10)   plot(x(times, myfit$argument), data)  # }

"none": states alone, Xf(). direction compiled separately. two second-order directions build "forward" well. call asks derivative built error. forcings character, names forcings f. Default NULL. data given Xs() Xf(). events eventlist, data.frame accepted .eventlist(). Default NULL. Events defined also act sensitivities adjoint. fixed character, initial values parameters without sensitivities. Default NULL. modelname character, base name generated files symbols. Default "odemodel". Files name outdir overwritten. backend "cppDE" (default), "Sundials" "deSolve": integrators cppDE, CVODE(S) cppDE, deSolve cOde. verbose logical, print compiler output. Default FALSE. used backend = "deSolve". outdir directory generated sources shared objects. Default getOption("dMod2.outdir"), else working directory. backend = "deSolve" writes working directory ; outdir, also one set option, error. ... title: Prediction Function — prdfn
text: leading arguments depend class matched position name: prediction function: x(times, pars, ...), returning prdlist; observation function: g(, pars, ...) prdlist , returning prdlist; parameter transformation: p(pars, ...), returning list one parvec per condition; objective function: obj(pars, ...), returning objlist. pars named numeric vector. deriv attribute, output parameter transformation , derivatives taken respect parameters behind . composition called according resulting class: g * x * p prediction function, (g * x * p)(times, pars). arguments named: fixed: named numeric vector parameters enter evaluation without derivatives. Default NULL. deriv: TRUE (default) returns first derivatives respect pars. Every function chain built derivMode = "forward", see odemodel(), Y() P(). deriv2: TRUE returns second derivatives well. Default FALSE. Every function chain built derivMode = "forward-forward". hessian: objective functions , see table . Default NULL. sweep: objective functions . "forward" (default) propagates sensitivities chain; "reverse" computes gradient one backward pass, whose cost grow number parameters. "reverse" needs every function chain built derivMode = "reverse", "forward-reverse" deriv2 = TRUE. conditions: character vector, conditions evaluate. Default conditions function. env: environment intermediate results. Default NULL, new one. objective function stores prediction prediction returns environment attribute env. cores: number threads ODE solves residual kernel. Default getOption("dMod2.cores", 1L). Prediction, observation parameter functions accept hessian sweep ignore . deriv = TRUE objective function returns Hessian: hessian = "sparse" returns Gauss-Newton Hessian forward sweep sparse Matrix, assembled blocks conditions; trust() factorizes argument sparse takes sparse path, vcov() solves columns . hessian = "expected" returns, place Gauss-Newton Hessian forward sweep, expected (Fisher) information likelihood: 2 / sigma^2 prediction 4 / sigma^2 sigma per data point, positive semidefinite also error model depends parameters. Gauss-Newton Hessian keeps exact curvature loss prediction sigma, indefinite shows optimizer saddle. deriv = FALSE returns value alone.

code: # \donttest{ ## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed ## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error th <- datasets::Theoph th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject) subjects <- unique(th$Subject) data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,                                condition = th$Subject)) ## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5)))  ## data against the population (PRED) and individual (IPRED) prediction, with residuals pr <- predict(fit) head(pr) #>   condition group time name observed    sigma sigmaPRED    IPRED     PRED #> 1         1     1 0.00    y     0.74 0.694404  0.694404 0.000000 0.000000 #> 2         1     1 0.25    y     2.84 0.694404  0.694404 3.845625 3.262278 #> 3         1     1 0.57    y     6.57 0.694404  0.694404 6.784953 5.829128 #> 4         1     1 1.12    y    10.50 0.694404  0.694404 9.043486 7.864023 #> 5         1     1 2.02    y     9.66 0.694404  0.694404 9.784612 8.504583 #> 6         1     1 3.82    y     8.58 0.694404  0.694404 9.093280 7.620456 #>   source       IRES       PRES      IWRES      PWRES #> 1    obs  0.7400000  0.7400000  1.0656621  1.0656621 #> 2    obs -1.0056252 -0.4222781 -1.4481847 -0.6081158 #> 3    obs -0.2149534  0.7408719 -0.3095509  1.0669177 #> 4    obs  1.4565144  2.6359772  2.0975030  3.7960283 #> 5    obs -0.1246117  1.1554172 -0.1794513  1.6638977 #> 6    obs -0.5132796  0.9595436 -0.7391657  1.3818233  ## the population prediction at additional times, here of the first subject grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 4) pop <- predict(fit, times = grid, type = "population") pop[pop$condition == "1" & pop$time %in% grid, ] #>    condition group time name observed sigmaPRED     PRED source PRES    PWRES #> 1          1     1    0    y     0.74  0.694404 0.000000    obs 0.74 1.065662 #> 42         1     1    4    y       NA  0.694404 7.508436   grid   NA       NA #> 55         1     1    8    y       NA  0.694404 5.325248   grid   NA       NA #> 66         1     1   12    y       NA  0.694404 3.767676   grid   NA       NA #> 70         1     1   16    y       NA  0.694404 2.665660   grid   NA       NA #> 71         1     1   20    y       NA  0.694404 1.885975   grid   NA       NA #> 74         1     1   24    y       NA  0.694404 1.334342   grid   NA       NA  ## observed against predicted, and data with the predicted curves per subject plot(fit)  plotCombined(fit)  # }

second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) init <- c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5))  ## FOCEI fit, the estimates and the random effects per subject fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init) fit #> EM (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations, 12 groups #>          Ka           V          Cl   sigma_add omega_Ka_Ka   omega_V_V  #>   0.4638825   3.4597479   1.0121568  -0.3647014  -0.4552240  -1.9774269  #> omega_Cl_Cl  #>  -1.3361153  #> Random effects: #>  type eta1 eta2  estimate         se #>    sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302 #>    sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699 #>    sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477 summary(fit) #> EM summary (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations #>   without the 2 pi constant of the data (NONMEM OBJ): 116.803413 #>  #> Parameters: #>             estimate      se rsePct #> Ka            0.4639 0.19180 41.350 #> V             3.4600 0.04718  1.364 #> Cl            1.0120 0.08333  8.233 #> sigma_add    -0.3647 0.07268 19.930 #> omega_Ka_Ka  -0.4552 0.23600 51.850 #> omega_V_V    -1.9770 0.29440 14.890 #> omega_Cl_Cl  -1.3360 0.25060 18.750 #> Standard errors without the curvature of the prediction in the random effects within the volume term (forward over reverse; derivMode = "forward-forward" gives the full one) #>  #> Random effects: #>  type eta1 eta2 estimate      se #>    sd   Ka   Ka   0.6343 0.14970 #>    sd    V    V   0.1384 0.04076 #>    sd   Cl   Cl   0.2629 0.06586 #>  #> Shrinkage: eta_Ka = 0.018, eta_V = 0.103, eta_Cl = 0.039  fit$omega #>   type eta1 eta2  estimate         se #> 1   sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302 #> 2   sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699 #> 3   sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477 head(fit$random) #>   group eta parameter        mode        se #> 1     1  Ka  eta_Ka_1  0.08621976 0.1515854 #> 2     2  Ka  eta_Ka_2  0.19818408 0.1725709 #> 3     3  Ka  eta_Ka_3  0.37186008 0.1810720 #> 4     4  Ka  eta_Ka_4 -0.28173371 0.1640986 #> 5     5  Ka  eta_Ka_5 -0.04271272 0.1461175 #> 6     6  Ka  eta_Ka_6 -0.38568935 0.2043190  ## quadrature started from the FOCEI estimates, and SAEM fitQ <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = fit, method = "quadrature", verbose = FALSE) fitS <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, method = "saem", verbose = FALSE) c(focei = fit$value, quadrature = fitQ$value, saem = fitS$value) #>      focei quadrature       saem  #>   359.4032   360.7089   360.7384  # } if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Ka and Cl with correlated random effects, V with a spike-and-slab one: a second transformation p2 <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID), V ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()))),         method = "explicit", compile = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_p2", derivMode = dm,         outdir = tempdir()) compile(p2, output = tempfile("theoph")) fit2 <- em(normL2(data, g * x * p2, errmodel = err), randomEffects(p2), init = init) fit2$omega fit2$slab AIC(fit, fit2) } # }

code: # Generate eqnlist from the constructor S <- matrix(c(-1, 1, 1, -1),             nrow = 2, ncol = 2,             dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B")))  rates <- c("k1*A", "k2*B") description <- c("forward", "backward")  f <- eqnlist(smatrix = S, rates = rates, description = description) print(f) #> Conserved quantities: #>   total_1 = 1*A+1*B #>  #>   Check Educt -> Product Rate Description #> 1           A ->       B k1*A     forward #> 2           B ->       A k2*B    backward  # Convert to data.frame fdata <- as.data.frame(f) print(fdata) #>   Description Rate  A  B #> 1     forward k1*A -1  1 #> 2    backward k2*B  1 -1  # Flat `volumes`: each distinct expression becomes a compartment c1, c2, ... f <- as.eqnlist(fdata, volumes = c(A = "Vcyt", B = "Vnuc")) print(f) #> Conserved quantities: #>   total_1 = 1*Vcyt*A+1*Vnuc*B #>  #> Compartments: #>   c1 (V=Vcyt) #>   c2 (V=Vnuc) #> States by compartment: #>   c1: A #>   c2: B #>  #>   Check Educt -> Product Rate Description #> 1           A ->       B k1*A     forward #> 2           B ->       A k2*B    backward print(as.eqnvec(f)) #> Idx Inner <- Outer #>   1     A <- -1*(k1*A)+1*(k2*B)*(Vnuc/Vcyt) #>   2     B <- 1*(k1*A)*(Vcyt/Vnuc)-1*(k2*B) print(as.eqnvec(f, type = "amount")) #> Idx Inner <- Outer #>   1     A <- -1*(k1*A)*(Vcyt)+1*(k2*B)*(Vnuc) #>   2     B <- 1*(k1*A)*(Vcyt)-1*(k2*B)*(Vnuc)  # Named compartments with explicit state assignment f2 <- eqnlist(   smatrix = S, rates = rates, description = description,   compartments = list(cyt = "Vcyt", nuc = "Vnuc"),   compartmentOf = c(A = "cyt", B = "nuc") ) print(f2) #> Conserved quantities: #>   total_1 = 1*Vcyt*A+1*Vnuc*B #>  #> Compartments: #>   cyt (V=Vcyt) #>   nuc (V=Vnuc) #> States by compartment: #>   cyt: A #>   nuc: B #>  #>   Check Educt -> Product Rate Description #> 1           A ->       B k1*A     forward #> 2           B ->       A k2*B    backward print(as.eqnvec(f2)) #> Idx Inner <- Outer #>   1     A <- -1*(k1*A)+1*(k2*B)*(Vnuc/Vcyt) #>   2     B <- 1*(k1*A)*(Vcyt/Vnuc)-1*(k2*B)

code: # \donttest{ ## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed ## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error th <- datasets::Theoph th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject) subjects <- unique(th$Subject) data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,                                condition = th$Subject)) ## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5)))  ## residuals in the order of the data rows of predict() pr <- predict(fit) pr <- pr[pr$source == "obs", ] head(data.frame(pr[c("condition", "time", "observed", "IPRED", "PRED")],                 IWRES = residuals(fit), CWRES = residuals(fit, type = "CWRES"),                 PWRES = residuals(fit, type = "PWRES"))) #>   condition time observed    IPRED     PRED      IWRES      CWRES      PWRES #> 1         1 0.00     0.74 0.000000 0.000000  1.0656621  1.0656621  1.0656621 #> 2         1 0.25     2.84 3.845625 3.262278 -1.4481847 -0.1771436 -0.6081158 #> 3         1 0.57     6.57 6.784953 5.829128 -0.3095509  1.0950932  1.0669177 #> 4         1 1.12    10.50 9.043486 7.864023  2.0975030  2.3313980  3.7960283 #> 5         1 2.02     9.66 9.784612 8.504583 -0.1794513 -0.6321836  1.6638977 #> 6         1 3.82     8.58 9.093280 7.620456 -0.7391657 -0.3220713  1.3818233  ## NPDE from 200 simulated data sets, with the tests of mean, variance and normality npde <- residuals(fit, type = "NPDE", nsim = 200, seed = 1) attr(npde, "tests") #>        test statistic           p #> 1      mean 0.8845372 0.378026872 #> 2  variance 0.8560526 0.236255368 #> 3 normality 0.9643513 0.001549586 #> 4    global        NA 0.004648758 # }

title: Summarize a mixed-effects fit — summary.em
code: # \donttest{ ## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed ## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error th <- datasets::Theoph th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject) subjects <- unique(th$Subject) data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,                                condition = th$Subject)) ## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) init <- c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5))  ## FOCEI fit, the estimates and the random effects per subject fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init) fit #> EM (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations, 12 groups #>          Ka           V          Cl   sigma_add omega_Ka_Ka   omega_V_V  #>   0.4638825   3.4597479   1.0121568  -0.3647014  -0.4552240  -1.9774269  #> omega_Cl_Cl  #>  -1.3361153  #> Random effects: #>  type eta1 eta2  estimate         se #>    sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302 #>    sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699 #>    sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477 summary(fit) #> EM summary (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations #>   without the 2 pi constant of the data (NONMEM OBJ): 116.803413 #>  #> Parameters: #>             estimate      se rsePct #> Ka            0.4639 0.19180 41.350 #> V             3.4600 0.04718  1.364 #> Cl            1.0120 0.08333  8.233 #> sigma_add    -0.3647 0.07268 19.930 #> omega_Ka_Ka  -0.4552 0.23600 51.850 #> omega_V_V    -1.9770 0.29440 14.890 #> omega_Cl_Cl  -1.3360 0.25060 18.750 #> Standard errors without the curvature of the prediction in the random effects within the volume term (forward over reverse; derivMode = "forward-forward" gives the full one) #>  #> Random effects: #>  type eta1 eta2 estimate      se #>    sd   Ka   Ka   0.6343 0.14970 #>    sd    V    V   0.1384 0.04076 #>    sd   Cl   Cl   0.2629 0.06586 #>  #> Shrinkage: eta_Ka = 0.018, eta_V = 0.103, eta_Cl = 0.039  fit$omega #>   type eta1 eta2  estimate         se #> 1   sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302 #> 2   sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699 #> 3   sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477 head(fit$random) #>   group eta parameter        mode        se #> 1     1  Ka  eta_Ka_1  0.08621976 0.1515854 #> 2     2  Ka  eta_Ka_2  0.19818408 0.1725709 #> 3     3  Ka  eta_Ka_3  0.37186008 0.1810720 #> 4     4  Ka  eta_Ka_4 -0.28173371 0.1640986 #> 5     5  Ka  eta_Ka_5 -0.04271272 0.1461175 #> 6     6  Ka  eta_Ka_6 -0.38568935 0.2043190  ## quadrature started from the FOCEI estimates, and SAEM fitQ <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = fit, method = "quadrature", verbose = FALSE) fitS <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, method = "saem", verbose = FALSE) c(focei = fit$value, quadrature = fitQ$value, saem = fitS$value) #>      focei quadrature       saem  #>   359.4032   360.7089   360.7537  # } if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Ka and Cl with correlated random effects, V with a spike-and-slab one: a second transformation p2 <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID), V ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()))),         method = "explicit", compile = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_p2", derivMode = dm,         outdir = tempdir()) compile(p2, output = tempfile("theoph")) fit2 <- em(normL2(data, g * x * p2, errmodel = err), randomEffects(p2), init = init) fit2$omega fit2$slab AIC(fit, fit2) } # }

code: rosenbrock <- function(x, ...) {   a <- x[["a"]]   b <- x[["b"]]   list(value = 100 * (b - a^2)^2 + (1 - a)^2,        gradient = c(a = -400 * a * (b - a^2) - 2 * (1 - a),                     b = 200 * (b - a^2)),        hessian = matrix(c(1200 * a^2 - 400 * b + 2, -400 * a, -400 * a, 200),                         2, 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b"), c("a", "b")))) }  fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), iterlim = 200) fit$argument #> a b  #> 1 1  fit$stopReason #> [1] "fvalue"  # With an upper bound on a fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), parupper = c(a = 0.5),              iterlim = 200) fit$atBound #>     a     b  #>  TRUE FALSE   # Gauss-Newton, then BFGS with a separate budget, then Gauss-Newton again fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), iterlim = 200,              phases = list(list(hessianMethod = "gn"),                            list(hessianMethod = "bfgs", iterlim = 50)),              switches = 2) fit$phaseIterations #>   gn bfgs  #>   26    0  fit$evalBySource #>      gn    bfgs     sr1   exact   sbfgs    ssr1 gnsbfgs  gnssr1  #>      27       0       0       0       0       0       0       0

second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em() dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse") x <- Xt() g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),        states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,        outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_obs.cpp err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,          derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) #> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpEh2W6Q/theoph_err.cpp ## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter ## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects] trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),                 table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects)) trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose) trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add")) p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,        modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir()) compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph")) #> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC] #> reusing 14 unchanged object(s) obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err) fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5)))  ##
